git.tip.detached.description: First line of the status bar's git tooltip. {commit} is a short commit hash.

git.tip.fetched.defaultMessage: As of the last fetch, {when}. Combwork never fetches by itself.
git.tip.fetched.description: The status bar's git tooltip. {when} is how long ago, such as "5m ago".

git.tip.gone.defaultMessage: It tracked {upstream}, which is gone from the remote.
git.tip.gone.description: The status bar's git tooltip. {upstream} is the remote branch, such as origin/main.

git.tip.neverFetched.defaultMessage: Never fetched: Combwork never fetches by itself.
git.tip.neverFetched.description: The status bar's git tooltip, when the repository was never fetched.

git.tip.noCommits.description: First line of the status bar's git tooltip, in a repository with no commit yet.

git.tip.noRemotes.description: The status bar's git tooltip: the repository has no remote.

git.tip.noTracking.defaultMessage: It tracks no remote branch: Push sets one.
git.tip.noTracking.description: The status bar's git tooltip. Push is the Git tab's button.

git.tip.on.description: First line of the status bar's git tooltip: the branch checked out.

git.tip.state.defaultMessage: Git is {state, select, merge {merging} rebase {rebasing} cherrypick {cherry-picking} revert {reverting} other {bisecting}}: finish or abort it in a terminal.
git.tip.state.description: The status bar's git tooltip, while git has an operation in progress in the project folder.

git.tip.tracks.defaultMessage: Tracks {upstream}: {ahead, plural, =0 {nothing} one {# commit} other {# commits}} to push, {behind, plural, =0 {nothing} one {# commit} other {# commits}} to pull.
git.tip.tracks.description: The status bar's git tooltip. {upstream} is the remote branch, such as origin/main; the counts are as of the last fetch.

git.tool.fixMissing.defaultMessage: Install Git for Windows ({min} or later), or add the folder holding git.exe to your PATH, then Check again in Provider Setup (no need to restart Combwork).
git.tool.fixMissing.description: How to fix git missing. {min} is a git version; Check again is a button in Provider Setup.

git.tool.fixOld.defaultMessage: Update Git for Windows to {min} or later, then Check again in Provider Setup.
git.tool.fixOld.description: How to fix a git that is too old. {min} is a git version; Check again is a button in Provider Setup.

git.tool.missing.defaultMessage: Git isn't installed (or isn't on Combwork's PATH)
git.tool.missing.description: Said wherever git is needed when Combwork cannot run git. No full stop: some places add more after it.

git.tool.oldLoses.defaultMessage: {lost, select, recent {With Git {version}: merging can't check for conflicts before it starts (the merge still stops at one); squash-merged branches still count as unmerged, so Remove All and loading a template keep their worktrees; the merge-ready skill can't check a branch for conflicts.} older {With Git {version}: merging can't check for conflicts before it starts (the merge still stops at one); squash-merged branches still count as unmerged, so Remove All and loading a template keep their worktrees; the merge-ready skill can't check a branch for conflicts; moving a workspace can't repair its worktrees.} other {With Git {version}: merging can't check for conflicts before it starts (the merge still stops at one); squash-merged branches still count as unmerged, so Remove All and loading a template keep their worktrees; the merge-ready skill can't check a branch for conflicts; Remove All and loading a template keep the branches of the worktrees they remove; moving a workspace can't repair its worktrees.}}
git.tool.oldLoses.description: Provider Setup: what does not work with an older git that still runs. {version} is its version; {lost} says how old it is (the older, the more is listed). Remove All and merge-ready are names in Combwork.

git.tool.tooOld.defaultMessage: Git {version} is too old for Combwork (it needs {min} or later)
git.tool.tooOld.description: Said wherever git is needed when the installed git is too old to run. {version} and {min} are git versions. No full stop: some places add more after it.

git.tool.tooOldToRun.defaultMessage: Combwork's git commands fail with Git {version}: worktrees, merging, the Version Control tab's Git sections and the unmerged counts don't work.
git.tool.tooOldToRun.description: Provider Setup, for a git too old for any of Combwork's git commands. {version} is its version.

git.track.about.defaultMessage: {tracks, select, yes {{branch} tracks {upstream} now. Pull and Push use the remote branch it tracks; other remotes stay as they are, and Push to… still pushes there.} other {{branch} tracks no remote branch now. Pull and Push use the remote branch it tracks; other remotes stay as they are, and Push to… still pushes there.}}
git.track.about.description: The Track form. {branch} is the local branch; {upstream} the remote branch it tracks now ({tracks} is no when none). Pull, Push and Push to… are buttons: keep their names.

git.track.pushFirst.defaultMessage: {remote} has no {branch} yet, as of the last fetch: Track pushes {local} there first (never forced).
git.track.pushFirst.description: Under the Track form when the chosen remote branch isn't known to exist. {remote} the remote, {branch} the branch name there, {local} the local branch.

git.track.remoteBranch.description: Field of the Track form: the branch's name on the remote.

git.track.tip.defaultMessage: Track…: choose the remote branch {branch} pulls from and pushes to
git.track.tip.description: Tooltip on a branch's Track… button. {branch} is the local branch.

git.track.title.description: Title of the Track form. {branch} is the local branch.

git.untrack.button.description: The button of the confirmation before a branch stops tracking its remote branch.

git.untrack.message.defaultMessage: {branch} no longer tracks a remote branch: Pull has nothing to pull from, and Push asks where to push it. Nothing changes on the remote.
git.untrack.message.description: The confirmation before a branch stops tracking its remote branch. Pull and Push are buttons: keep their names.

git.untrack.tip.description: Tooltip on a branch's stop-tracking button. {upstream} is the remote branch it tracks.

git.untrack.title.description: Title of the confirmation before a branch stops tracking its remote branch.

git.update.agents.defaultMessage: {agents} {n, plural, one {works} other {work}} there: {n, plural, one {its} other {their}} next turn starts from the updated branch.
git.update.agents.description: The Update from <target> dialog: agents ({agents}: their names, joined) work in the folder the update runs in, none in a turn now; what they do next starts from the updated branch.

git.update.approval.defaultMessage: {approval, select, carries {{card} has passed review: its pass carries over when the update is the same change, as a clean merge or rebase is.} other {{card} has passed review: once updated, it goes back for review (the project keeps a pass only for the exact commit).}}
git.update.approval.description: The Update from <target> dialog, for a card that passed review ({card}: its key): whether the pass survives the update (carries: the project's "A pass survives a clean rebase" is on; other: the card is reviewed again). Select: translate each.

git.update.behind.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {# commit of {target} it hasn't} other {# commits of {target} it hasn't}}
git.update.behind.description: On a branch in Version Control → Branches & remotes (HI-1180): how many commits of the target branch {target} the branch doesn't have yet (Update from {target} brings them in).

git.update.busy.description: The Update from <target> dialog's button while the branch is being updated.

git.update.card.description: The Update from <target> dialog: the branch is the line of a card ({card}: its key, such as HI-12) that isn't Done.

git.update.confirm.description: The Update from <target> dialog's button: updates the branch.

git.update.counts.defaultMessage: {target} has {behind, plural, one {# commit} other {# commits}} {branch} hasn't; {branch} has {ahead, plural, one {# commit} other {# commits}} of its own.
git.update.counts.description: The Update from <target> dialog's first sentence: how many commits of the target {target} the branch {branch} lacks ({behind}), and how many it has that the target hasn't ({ahead}).

git.update.forward.description: The one choice in the Update from <target> dialog for a branch with no commits of its own (HI-1180): it is moved forward to the target branch {target}.

git.update.forwardNote.defaultMessage: {branch} has no commits of its own, so it simply moves forward to {target}: no merge commit, nothing rewritten.
git.update.forwardNote.description: What Fast-forward does, under the choice in the Update from <target> dialog: the branch {branch} has nothing the target {target} lacks, so it moves to the target.

git.update.how.description: A label in the Update from <target> dialog: the choice of Merge or Rebase.

git.update.merge.description: An option in the Update from <target> dialog (the default): merge the target branch {target} into the branch, as one merge commit.

git.update.mergeNote.defaultMessage: One merge commit joins {target}'s commits to {branch}'s, which stay as they are.
git.update.mergeNote.description: What Merge does, under the choice in the Update from <target> dialog: one merge commit; the branch {branch} keeps its own commits as they are.

git.update.planFailed.defaultMessage: Couldn't read what updating {branch} would do
git.update.planFailed.description: An error notification's title (HI-1180): reading what Update from <target> would do to the branch {branch} failed.

git.update.rebase.description: An option in the Update from <target> dialog: replay the branch's own commits on top of the target branch {target}.

git.update.rebaseNote.defaultMessage: {branch}'s {n, plural, one {commit is} other {# commits are}} replayed on top of {target}, as new commits.{pushed, select, yes { What was pushed of {branch} then differs from it, and Combwork never forces a push.} other {}}
git.update.rebaseNote.description: What Rebase does, under the choice in the Update from <target> dialog: the branch's {n} commits are rewritten on top of {target}; with pushed yes, it tracks a remote branch, which then no longer matches (pushing it would need a force, which Combwork never does).

git.update.tip.description: Tooltip on a branch's Update button in Version Control → Branches & remotes (HI-1180): merges the target {target} into the branch {branch}, or rebases it onto {target} (a dialog asks which first).

git.update.title.description: Title of the Update from <target> dialog (HI-1180): bring the branch {branch} up to date with the target branch {target}.

git.update.undone.defaultMessage: A conflict is undone at once, leaving {branch} as it was.
git.update.undone.description: The Update from <target> dialog: if git stops at a conflict, Combwork aborts the merge or rebase, so the branch {branch} is never left half updated.

git.update.where.defaultMessage: {where, select, project {It runs in the project folder, where {branch} is checked out.} slot {It runs in {slot}, the slot {branch} is checked out in.} worktree {It runs in {folder}, where {branch} is checked out.} other {{branch} is checked out nowhere: Combwork updates it in a temporary folder, removed after.}}
git.update.where.description: The Update from <target> dialog: where the update runs (select: translate each): the project folder, a slot ({slot}: its name, such as slot-a), another worktree ({folder}: its path), or a temporary folder Combwork makes when the branch isn't checked out anywhere.

git.upstream.gone.description: In place of the ahead/behind counts: the remote branch a branch tracked was deleted on the remote.

git.validate.enterName.description: Under a form's name box (a remote, a branch, a tag) while it is empty.

git.validate.enterUrl.description: Under a remote's URL box while it is empty.

git.validate.nameLine.defaultMessage: A name is one line, without < or >
git.validate.nameLine.description: Under a commit identity form when the name has a line break, < or >.

git.validate.notUrl.defaultMessage: That isn't a URL or path

git.validate.remoteName.description: Under Add a remote's name box when the name has other characters.

git.validate.wholeUrl.defaultMessage: Type the whole URL: its password or token is hidden here
git.validate.wholeUrl.description: Under a remote's URL box when it still has ••• for a hidden password.

git.vc.choice.description: Accessible name of the None · Git choice atop the Version Control tab (glossary 2.1: version control).

git.vc.fact.gone.defaultMessage: The Git repository is gone from this folder. Until it’s back, what needs Git can’t be read.
git.vc.fact.gone.description: Atop the Version Control tab of a Git project whose .git was removed or moved.

git.vc.fact.jj.defaultMessage: This folder is a jj repository at {root}, {colocated, select, yes {colocated with Git} other {not colocated with Git}}.
git.vc.fact.jj.description: Atop the Version Control tab (HI-2799, HI-2896): what Combwork found in the project folder, a jj (Jujutsu) repository. {root} is its root; colocated with Git means a .git folder beside .jj, not colocated that Git’s data is inside .jj (both are supported). Keep jj and Git.

git.vc.fact.jjGone.defaultMessage: The jj repository is gone from this folder.
git.vc.fact.jjGone.description: Atop the Version Control tab of a project using jj (Jujutsu, HI-2799) whose .jj folder was removed or moved. Keep jj.

git.vc.fact.jjInGit.defaultMessage: This folder is a jj repository at {root}, not colocated, inside the Git repository at {git}: Combwork can’t use jj here.
git.vc.fact.jjInGit.description: Atop the Version Control tab (HI-2896): a jj (Jujutsu) repository whose Git data is inside .jj, in a folder that is itself inside a Git working tree ({git}); git commands in it would reach that repository, so jj isn’t offered. Keep jj and Git.

git.vc.fact.none.defaultMessage: This folder has no version control.
git.vc.fact.none.description: Atop the Version Control tab, when the project folder has no repository.

git.vc.fact.other.defaultMessage: {vcs} found: not supported yet, so this project uses None.
git.vc.fact.other.description: Atop the Version Control tab: another version control was found in the folder. {vcs} is its name (Mercurial, Jujutsu). None: glossary 2.1.

git.vc.fact.otherGit.defaultMessage: {vcs} found in this folder: not supported yet.
git.vc.fact.otherGit.description: Atop the Version Control tab of a project still using Git, where another version control was found ({vcs}: Mercurial, Jujutsu). The offer under it says what to do.

git.vc.fact.repo.defaultMessage: This folder is a Git repository at {root}.
git.vc.fact.repo.description: Atop the Version Control tab: what Combwork found in the project folder. {root} is the repository root (glossary 2.1: repository root).

git.vc.fact.subfolder.defaultMessage: This folder is inside a Git repository at {root}: branch and merge actions affect that whole repository.
git.vc.fact.subfolder.description: Atop the Version Control tab, when the project is a subfolder of a larger repository. {root} is that repository’s root.

git.vc.git.description: A version control system’s name, in the choice atop the Version Control tab (glossary 2.1: keep).

git.vc.initHint.defaultMessage: Initialise repository… makes this folder a Git repository on a branch called main, keeps its .combwork out of git and commits its files.
git.vc.initHint.description: Under the header of the Version Control tab of a project whose folder has no repository, beside the button. Initialise repository… is the button’s name: keep it as translated there. Keep main (the branch name).

git.vc.initOwnHint.defaultMessage: Initialise its own repository… makes this folder a Git repository of its own on a branch called main, keeps its .combwork out of git and commits its files.
git.vc.initOwnHint.description: Git’s page in the Version Control tab of a project inside another repository, under its buttons. Initialise its own repository… is the button’s name: keep it as translated there. Keep main (the branch name).

git.vc.insideRepo.defaultMessage: This folder is inside the Git repository at {root}: use that one, or give this folder its own.
git.vc.insideRepo.description: Git’s page in the Version Control tab of a project inside another repository, chosen before it has its own: above the buttons Use that repository… and Initialise its own repository…. {root} is the outer repository’s folder.

git.vc.jj.description: Jujutsu’s command name, as its users call it, in the choice atop the Version Control tab (HI-2799). Keep it: a product’s name, lower case.

git.vc.noCommitYet.defaultMessage: This folder's Git repository has no first commit yet.
git.vc.noCommitYet.description: Git’s page in the Version Control tab, when Initialise repository… made the repository but stopped before its first commit: above the Make first commit… button.

git.vc.none.description: The version control of a project without any, in the choice atop the Version Control tab and in "Workflow: None · Solo" (glossary 2.1: None).

git.vc.notRepoYet.defaultMessage: This folder isn't a Git repository yet.
git.vc.notRepoYet.description: Git’s page in the Version Control tab of a project whose folder has no repository, chosen before it has one: above the Initialise repository… button.

git.vc.offer.gitFound.defaultMessage: Git found at {root}: switch to Git?
git.vc.offer.gitFound.description: An offer atop the Version Control tab of a project without version control, after someone ran git init: {root} is the repository root. Combwork never switches by itself.

git.vc.offer.jjFound.defaultMessage: jj found at {root}: switch to jj?
git.vc.offer.jjFound.description: An offer atop the Version Control tab (HI-2799, HI-2896): a jj (Jujutsu) repository, colocated with Git or not, was found in the project folder. Combwork never switches by itself. Keep jj.

git.vc.offer.jjGone.defaultMessage: The jj repository is gone: switch this project back to {platform}?
git.vc.offer.jjGone.description: An offer atop the Version Control tab of a project using jj (HI-2799) whose .jj folder is gone. {platform} is Git or None. Keep jj.

git.vc.offer.notNow.description: A button of the offer to switch version control (atop the Version Control tab): hides the offer until Combwork starts again.

git.vc.offer.otherFound.defaultMessage: {vcs} found: not supported yet, so this project can only use None.
git.vc.offer.otherFound.description: An offer atop the Version Control tab of a Git project where another version control ({vcs}: Mercurial, Jujutsu) is found now. None: glossary 2.1.

git.vc.offer.repositoryGone.defaultMessage: The Git repository is gone. Git’s rules hold until you switch, because what they check can’t be read.
git.vc.offer.repositoryGone.description: An offer atop the Version Control tab of a Git project whose .git folder was removed or moved: its cards are refused until the user switches to None or the repository is back.

git.vc.offer.switchGit.description: A button of the offer to switch a project to Git (atop the Version Control tab): shows what changes, then asks. The … says it asks first: keep it.

git.vc.offer.switchJj.description: A button of the offer to switch a project to jj (Jujutsu, HI-2799): shows what changes, then asks. The … says it asks first: keep it. Keep jj.

git.vc.offer.switchNone.description: A button of the offer to switch a project to None, no version control (atop the Version Control tab): shows what changes, then asks. The … says it asks first: keep it. None: glossary 2.1.

git.vc.previewTip.defaultMessage: Git needs this folder to be a repository: Initialise repository… makes it one. Nothing changes until you do.
git.vc.previewTip.description: Tooltip of Git in the None · Git choice atop the Version Control tab of a project whose folder has no repository of its own: clicking it shows Git’s page, which only offers Initialise repository… (keep it as translated on that button).

git.vc.sections.description: Accessible name of the Version Control tab's row of sections (Workflow, Changes, History…). Glossary 2.1: Version Control (the tab).

git.vc.step.cantSave.defaultMessage: This preset can’t be saved for the project:
git.vc.step.cantSave.description: Before the reasons a preset can’t be saved (it contradicts the workspace’s options, say), in the "How do you work?" step.

git.vc.step.choose.description: The step’s main button: saves the preset shown ({preset}: Solo, Pair, Team) as the project’s workflow options, after a confirmation.

git.vc.step.confirmTitle.description: Title of the confirmation after Choose in the "How do you work?" step. {preset} is Solo, Pair or Team; {project} the project’s name.

git.vc.step.customise.description: A button of the "How do you work?" step: opens the Workflow section with the preset shown filled in, not saved. The … says more follows: keep it.

git.vc.step.details.description: A link in the "How do you work?" step: shows each option the preset shown ({preset}: Solo, Pair, Team) sets, and why.

git.vc.step.hideDetails.description: The link in the "How do you work?" step once the preset’s options are shown: hides them again. {preset} is Solo, Pair or Team.

git.vc.step.intro.defaultMessage: A preset sets up this project’s workflow in one click: who reviews the work, which checks pass first and who merges. Nothing changes until you choose.
git.vc.step.intro.description: Under "How do you work?": what choosing a preset does (glossary 2.1: preset, workflow).

git.vc.step.introNone.defaultMessage: A preset sets up this project’s workflow in one click: who reviews the work and which checks pass first. Nothing changes until you choose.
git.vc.step.introNone.description: Under "How do you work?" for a project without version control (None): what choosing a preset does. None has no merging, so unlike the Git intro it names no merges (glossary 2.1: preset, workflow).

git.vc.step.keeps.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {The card in flight keeps the rules it started with; the options apply from the next card.} other {The # cards in flight keep the rules they started with; the options apply from the next card.}}
git.vc.step.keeps.description: The confirmation after Choose in the "How do you work?" step, when cards have started (glossary: old rules).

git.vc.step.notNow.description: A button of the "How do you work?" step: no preset; the options stay inherited and the step isn’t offered again for this version control.

git.vc.step.nothing.defaultMessage: Nothing is in flight yet: its options apply from the first card that starts.
git.vc.step.nothing.description: The confirmation after Choose in the "How do you work?" step, when no card has started and no lane runs.

git.vc.step.presets.description: Accessible name of the row of presets (Solo, Pair, Team) in the "How do you work?" step.

git.vc.step.saved.description: A notice after a preset was chosen in the "How do you work?" step.

git.vc.step.suggested.description: A tag on the preset Combwork suggests for the project, in the "How do you work?" step.

git.vc.step.title.description: The heading of the step that offers a new project a preset (Solo, Pair, Team), atop its Version Control tab.

git.vc.step.use.description: The confirm button after Choose in the "How do you work?" step. {preset} is Solo, Pair or Team.

git.vc.step.why.defaultMessage: {why, select, solo {Suggested for one agent or none.} pair {Suggested for a builder and a reviewer.} other {Suggested for more agents than a builder and a reviewer.}}
git.vc.step.why.description: Why Combwork suggests the marked preset, from the project’s agents, in the "How do you work?" step. Keep the select keys.

git.vc.stepNotice.choose.description: A button of the notice for projects added without a workflow: opens the first one’s Version Control tab at "How do you work?". The … says more follows: keep it.

git.vc.stepNotice.notNow.description: A button of the notice for projects added without a workflow: answers "How do you work?" with Not now for each (their options stay inherited), so it isn’t shown again.

git.vc.stepNotice.text.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {{projects} was added: how do you work?} other {{projects} were added: how do you work?}} A preset sets up a workflow in one click.
git.vc.stepNotice.text.description: A notice for projects Combwork found in the workspace (or the Assistant added) that have no workflow yet: it offers the "How do you work?" step (glossary 2.1: preset, workflow). {projects} is a list of project names; {n} how many.

git.vc.store.autocrlf.defaultMessage: Git converts line endings here (core.autocrlf). If this repository doesn’t need that, turn it off for it alone: run {command} in it, then Check Again.
git.vc.store.autocrlf.description: Under Git attributes in the warning before switching to jj (HI-2872), when Git’s line-ending conversion is on. {command} is a git command, kept as it is; core.autocrlf is a Git setting; Check Again is the dialog’s button.

git.vc.store.card.description: A card started and not done, in the switch’s warning (HI-2799). {card} is its key.

git.vc.store.carried.defaultMessage: {what, select, line {{project}: {card}’s work from before is on {line}{state, select, ahead {, with commits its target doesn’t hold} other {, and Combwork couldn’t tell whether its target holds it}}. After the switch {card} starts from its target, not that line: if its target doesn’t hold that work by then, bring it in yourself.} card {{project}: Combwork couldn’t read {card}’s earlier starts, so it can’t tell whether work from before is left on a line of its own. After the switch {card} starts from its target: check before you start it.} other {{project}: Combwork couldn’t read its cards’ earlier starts, so it can’t tell whether any has work from before left on a line of its own. After the switch they start from their target: check before you start them.}}
git.vc.store.carried.description: HI-3107: a hint in the warning before switching to jj. line: a card not in flight ran before under Git, and its branch from then has (ahead) or may have (other: it couldn’t be read) work its target lacks; the card will start from its target, not that branch. card: that card’s earlier starts couldn’t be read; other: the project’s board couldn’t be read. Keep the select keys. {card} is a card key; {line} a branch name.

git.vc.store.clear.description: A feature jj doesn’t support, not used by this repository (HI-2799). {gate} is its name.

git.vc.store.conflictedBookmark.defaultMessage: Bookmark {name} is conflicted: resolve it with jj.
git.vc.store.conflictedBookmark.description: Why a jj project can’t go back to Git yet (HI-2799): a bookmark points at several commits. Keep jj.

git.vc.store.conflictedCommit.defaultMessage: Commit {commit} stores conflicts: resolve them with jj.
git.vc.store.conflictedCommit.description: Why a jj project can’t go back to Git yet (HI-2799): a commit on a bookmark stores unresolved conflicts. {commit} is a short id. Keep jj.

git.vc.store.copy.description: In the switch’s warning (HI-2799): a review or check copy still in use.

git.vc.store.detached.defaultMessage: {project}: its folder is on no branch (its head is detached at {head}), and stays so after the switch. Check out the branch its work goes on there (git switch) before its cards start in the project folder.
git.vc.store.detached.description: HI-3104: a hint in the warning before switching back to Git: a project’s folder has no branch checked out (a detached head, as a jj repository colocated with Git leaves it). Combwork doesn’t check one out; a card started in that folder is refused until the user does. {head} is a short commit id. git switch is a command: keep it.

git.vc.store.drain.defaultMessage: Still running on this repository (the switch waits until all of it has finished):
git.vc.store.drain.description: In the warning before switching between Git and jj (HI-2799): above what still uses the repository. Nothing of it is stopped by Combwork.

git.vc.store.fallback.description: In the warning before switching a jj project back to Git (HI-2799): above what isn’t ready. Keep Git.

git.vc.store.fallbackUnknown.description: Why a jj project can’t go back to Git yet (HI-2799): jj couldn’t be read. {detail} is a short code, kept in English.

git.vc.store.gates.defaultMessage: What this repository uses, checked for jj:
git.vc.store.gates.description: In the warning before switching to jj (HI-2799): above each Git feature jj doesn’t support, checked in this repository. Keep jj.

git.vc.store.group.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {This project switches:} other {These projects share this repository and switch together:}}
git.vc.store.group.description: In the warning before switching between Git and jj (HI-2799): above the projects of the workspace on the same repository, which all switch.

git.vc.store.heads.defaultMessage: jj has {n, plural, =0 {no readable operation head} one {# operation head} other {# operation heads}}: let jj reconcile them first.
git.vc.store.heads.description: Why a jj project can’t go back to Git yet (HI-2799): jj’s operation log has diverged. Keep jj.

git.vc.store.kept.defaultMessage: {project}: {card}’s committed work, kept in slot {slot} for when it starts again: start {card} and finish it
git.vc.store.kept.description: In the switch’s warning (HI-3069): a card was put back with commits, and its slot is kept for it; after the switch that slot could never be lent back, so the switch waits until the card has finished. {card} is a card key like AM-12; {slot} a slot’s name (glossary 2.5: slot).

git.vc.store.lane.description: A running lane in the switch’s warning (HI-2799). A noun before the name (glossary §1 rule 4).

git.vc.store.laneUnnamed.description: A running lane with no name in the switch’s warning (HI-2799).

git.vc.store.limit.description: A limit of jj in Combwork (HI-2799): its name and why.

git.vc.store.member.description: A project in the warning before switching between Git and jj (HI-2799). {platform} is None, Git or jj, its version control now.

git.vc.store.notExported.defaultMessage: Bookmark {name} isn’t the same in Git: run jj git export, or check it.
git.vc.store.notExported.description: Why a jj project can’t go back to Git yet (HI-2799): a bookmark and its Git branch differ. Keep jj git export (a command).

git.vc.store.queue.description: In the switch’s warning (HI-2799): a project’s merge queue still has work (glossary 2.5: merge queue).

git.vc.store.slot.description: In the switch’s warning (HI-2799): a slot (a card’s own folder) still lent to an agent (glossary 2.5: slot).

git.vc.store.stock.defaultMessage: Git for Windows’ own default settings (its LFS filter, the diff driver for Office documents) don’t count: only what the repository or your own Git settings use.
git.vc.store.stock.description: Under the gates in the warning before switching to jj (HI-2872): Git for Windows’ stock system settings are ignored. Keep Git for Windows (a product’s name) and LFS.

git.vc.store.stuck.defaultMessage: Combwork stopped while switching {projects} between Git and jj, and can’t tell from their settings which way to finish: {changed} changed or can’t be read. Until they show their version control from before or after the switch, nothing starts on their repository.
git.vc.store.stuck.description: HI-3073: a notice’s message. {projects} names the projects that were switching; {changed}, those whose project settings were changed by hand meanwhile or can’t be read. Keep Git and jj.

git.vc.store.stuckTitle.defaultMessage: A version control switch couldn’t be finished
git.vc.store.stuckTitle.description: HI-3073: a notice’s title. A switch between Git and jj was cut short (Combwork closed or crashed during it), and Combwork couldn’t settle it from the projects’ files, so the repository stays switching.

git.vc.store.toGit.defaultMessage: Combwork leaves .jj in place: remove it with jj if you no longer want it.
git.vc.store.toGit.description: In the warning before switching a jj project back to Git (HI-2799). Keep .jj and jj.

git.vc.store.toJj.defaultMessage: Combwork never creates a jj repository or changes how it is colocated: .jj, and .git where there is one, stay as they are. Cards run in slots of their own, and you integrate the reviewed work yourself: Combwork never moves a bookmark or pushes.
git.vc.store.toJj.description: In the warning before switching to jj (HI-2799, HI-2896: a jj repository colocated with Git has a .git beside .jj, one not colocated has none; HI-2874: jj cards run). A bookmark is jj’s name for a branch. Keep jj, .jj and .git.

git.vc.store.unknown.defaultMessage: {gate}: couldn’t be checked ({what}), so it counts as used
git.vc.store.unknown.description: A feature jj doesn’t support whose use Combwork couldn’t read (HI-2799): unreadable counts as used, so the switch is refused.

git.vc.store.unsupported.defaultMessage: Not supported with jj, whatever the repository:
git.vc.store.unsupported.description: In the warning before switching to jj (HI-2799): above what Combwork never does with jj (merging, pushing, moving…). Keep jj.

git.vc.store.uses.description: A feature jj doesn’t support, used by this repository (HI-2799): {what} says where (a setting, a file), as found.

git.vc.switch.changed.defaultMessage: Changed meanwhile: this project uses {platform} now. Look again before switching.
git.vc.switch.changed.description: Why a switch of version control was refused: someone else switched it since the tab was shown. {platform} is None, Git or jj.

git.vc.switch.checkAgain.description: The button of a refused switch between Git and jj (HI-2799): reads the repository and what runs on it again, and shows the warning again (or switches, after asking).

git.vc.switch.close.description: Closes the refused switch’s dialog (HI-2799) without switching.

git.vc.switch.confirm.description: The confirm button of the warning before switching a project’s version control.

git.vc.switch.done.description: A notice after switching a project’s version control. {project} is its name, {platform} None or Git.

git.vc.switch.drain.defaultMessage: Work is still running on this repository: switch once it has finished.
git.vc.switch.drain.description: Why a switch between Git and jj is refused (HI-2799): lanes, cards in flight, the merge queue or slots are still in use on the repository (listed in the same dialog). Keep Git and jj.

git.vc.switch.fallback.defaultMessage: The repository isn’t ready to go back to Git: see the list.
git.vc.switch.fallback.description: Why a jj project can’t be switched back to Git (HI-2799): conflicted bookmarks, changes Git hasn’t received and the like (listed in the same dialog). Keep Git.

git.vc.switch.fresh.defaultMessage: It has no {to} options of its own yet: they come from the workspace’s and Combwork’s defaults until you choose some. {from}’s are kept for a switch back.
git.vc.switch.fresh.description: In the warning before switching version control, when the project never used the other one: it starts with no options of its own (inherited). {to} and {from} are None or Git.

git.vc.switch.gates.defaultMessage: This repository uses what jj doesn’t support: see the list.
git.vc.switch.gates.description: Why a project can’t be switched to jj (HI-2799): the compatibility check found Git features jj doesn’t support (listed in the same dialog). Keep jj.

git.vc.switch.gitFolder.defaultMessage: This folder is still a Git repository, but with None Combwork records no commits or merges for its cards.
git.vc.switch.gitFolder.description: In the warning before switching a project to None (no version control) while its folder is a Git repository. None: glossary 2.1.

git.vc.switch.groupChanged.defaultMessage: This repository’s projects changed meanwhile: look again before switching.
git.vc.switch.groupChanged.description: Why a switch between Git and jj is refused (HI-2799): a project joined the repository, or one of its projects’ choices or options changed, after the warning was shown.

git.vc.switch.inFlight.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {This card in flight finishes under {from}’s rules (old rules):} other {These cards in flight finish under {from}’s rules (old rules):}}
git.vc.switch.inFlight.description: In the warning before switching version control, above the cards already started (glossary: old rules). {from} is None or Git. Unlike other option changes, a switch can’t be applied to them.

git.vc.switch.jjInGit.defaultMessage: This jj repository isn’t colocated with Git and sits inside the Git repository at {root}: git commands run here would change that repository. Move it out, or make it colocated with jj.
git.vc.switch.jjInGit.description: Why a project (or a card start, or a slot) can’t use jj (HI-2896): its jj repository keeps Git’s data inside .jj, and a folder above it is a Git working tree ({root}), which any git command in the project would reach. Keep jj and Git.

git.vc.switch.jjNoGitCopy.defaultMessage: No Git working copy here: this jj repository keeps Git’s data inside .jj. To go back to Git, make it colocated with jj (jj git colocation enable), then switch. Or choose None.
git.vc.switch.jjNoGitCopy.description: Why a jj project can’t be switched to Git (HI-2896): its jj repository isn’t colocated, so the folder has no .git. Keep jj, Git, None (glossary 2.1) and the command as it is.

git.vc.switch.jjTool.defaultMessage: {state, select, missing {jj isn’t installed (or isn’t on the PATH)} old {This jj is older than the one Combwork is tested with} untested {This jj is newer than the one Combwork is tested with} other {jj couldn’t be checked}}, so this project can’t use jj.
git.vc.switch.jjTool.description: Why a project can’t be switched to jj (HI-2799): the jj tool Combwork found. Keep jj.

git.vc.switch.jjToolBack.defaultMessage: {state, select, missing {jj isn’t installed (or isn’t on the PATH)} old {This jj is older than the one Combwork is tested with} untested {This jj is newer than the one Combwork is tested with} other {jj couldn’t be checked}}, so Combwork can’t check that this repository is ready to go back to Git. Install the jj Combwork is tested with, then switch. Or, if you’re done with jj, remove the .jj folder: the project can then go back to Git without it.
git.vc.switch.jjToolBack.description: Why a jj project can’t be switched back to Git (HI-2975): jj itself is missing or not the tested version, so whether its bookmarks reached Git can’t be checked. Keep jj, Git and .jj.

git.vc.switch.jjUnknown.defaultMessage: jj couldn’t confirm this repository ({code}), so this project can’t switch.
git.vc.switch.jjUnknown.description: Why a project can’t be switched to or from jj (HI-2799): jj didn’t confirm what its files say. {code} is a short code for why (kept in English). Keep jj.

git.vc.switch.lane.description: A running lane in the warning before switching version control. {builder} is the agent building its cards, {name} the lane’s name. A noun before the name (glossary §1 rule 4).

git.vc.switch.laneUnnamed.description: A running lane with no name in the warning before switching version control. {builder} is the agent building its cards. A noun before the name (glossary §1 rule 4).

git.vc.switch.lanes.defaultMessage: {n, plural, one {This running lane keeps {from}’s rules until it ends:} other {These running lanes keep {from}’s rules until they end:}}
git.vc.switch.lanes.description: In the warning before switching version control, above the lanes running now (glossary: lane, old rules). {from} is None or Git.

git.vc.switch.memberDrain.defaultMessage: Work is still running in this project. Its repository has been switched between Git and jj, so the project switches to None only once that work has finished.
git.vc.switch.memberDrain.description: Why a project can’t be switched to None now (HI-2974): its repository was once switched between Git and jj, and lanes, cards in flight, the merge queue, slots or review copies of this project are still in use (listed in the same dialog). Keep Git, jj and None (glossary 2.1).

git.vc.switch.memberNoJj.defaultMessage: {project} is on this repository, but its folder isn’t a jj workspace (a Git worktree, say), so it can’t use jj. Choose None for {project}, or remove it from the workspace, then switch.
git.vc.switch.memberNoJj.description: Why a switch to jj is refused (HI-3034): every project on the repository switches together, and {project}, another project on it, is a folder jj doesn’t know (typically a git worktree the user made). Keep jj, Git and None (glossary 2.1).

git.vc.switch.noGit.defaultMessage: No Git repository here: Initialise repository… first.
git.vc.switch.noGit.description: Why a project can’t be switched to Git (the Version Control tab’s choice, a refusal): its folder has no Git repository. Initialise repository… is a button’s name: keep it as translated there.

git.vc.switch.noJj.defaultMessage: No jj repository here. Combwork never makes one: create it with jj.
git.vc.switch.noJj.description: Why a project can’t be switched to jj (Jujutsu, HI-2799, HI-2896): its folder has no jj repository. Keep jj.

git.vc.switch.notSwitched.defaultMessage: {project} is a Git repository now, but it wasn't switched to Git: {error}
git.vc.switch.notSwitched.description: A notice after Initialise repository… chosen from Git’s page made the repository but switching the project to Git failed. {project} is its name, {error} why (already translated).

git.vc.switch.nothing.defaultMessage: Nothing is in flight: every card works under {to} from now.
git.vc.switch.nothing.description: In the warning before switching version control when no card has started and no lane runs. {to} is None or Git.

git.vc.switch.otherFound.defaultMessage: {vcs} found: not supported yet, so this project can only use None.
git.vc.switch.otherFound.description: Why a project can’t be switched to Git: another version control ({vcs}: Mercurial, Subversion) was found in its folder. None: glossary 2.1.

git.vc.switch.otherWorkspace.defaultMessage: This repository is also a project of the open workspace {workspace}: close it there first.
git.vc.switch.otherWorkspace.description: Why a switch between Git and jj is refused (HI-2799): another open workspace (another window) has a project on the same repository, whose work Combwork can’t hold while it switches. {workspace} is its name. Keep Git and jj.

git.vc.switch.queue.defaultMessage: Their merge queue carries on, and stays in this tab and the Progress panel until it’s clear.
git.vc.switch.queue.description: In the warning before switching from Git to None, under the Git cards in flight: their merge queue goes on until it is empty.

git.vc.switch.restored.defaultMessage: The {to} options it had before come back as they were; {from}’s are kept for a switch back.
git.vc.switch.restored.description: In the warning before switching version control, when the project used the other one before: its options for it are restored. {to} and {from} are None or Git.

git.vc.switch.storeRuns.defaultMessage: This repository uses {platform} now (its other projects switched it), so this project can’t use Git on it: switch the repository back to Git from one of those projects first.
git.vc.switch.storeRuns.description: Why a project can’t be switched to Git (HI-3072): it is on a repository (a Git worktree of one, say) whose other projects switched it to jj, so a Git project there would mix Git and jj on one repository. {platform} is jj (or Git), as the window names it.

git.vc.switch.switching.defaultMessage: This repository’s version control is being switched: try again in a moment.
git.vc.switch.switching.description: Why a switch (or a start, a lane, a slot) is refused for now (HI-2799): another switch of the same repository between Git and jj is under way.

git.vc.switch.title.description: Title of the warning before switching a project’s version control. {project} is its name, {platform} None or Git.

git.vc.switch.what.defaultMessage: From its next card, {project} uses {to} and {to}’s own workflow options. Cards already started keep {from}’s rules.
git.vc.switch.what.description: The warning before switching a project’s version control: what changes. {to} and {from} are None or Git.

git.vc.switchTip.defaultMessage: Switch this project to {platform}, from its next card. Combwork shows what changes first.
git.vc.switchTip.description: Tooltip of the version control not in use, in the None · Git choice atop the Version Control tab: clicking it asks before switching. {platform} is None or Git.

git.vc.templateNotApplied.defaultMessage: {project} still uses None, so the Git workflow of {template} wasn’t applied. Switch the project to Git, then load the template again.
git.vc.templateNotApplied.description: A notice (HI-1910): the repository was made from Git’s page for a template ({template}) whose workflow needs Git, but the project ({project}) wasn’t switched to Git (refused, or the warning cancelled). None and Git as Combwork names them.

git.vc.templatePending.defaultMessage: For the template {template}: once the repository is made and this project uses Git, its Load dialog opens again.
git.vc.templatePending.description: Git’s page in the Version Control tab (HI-1910), opened from the Load template dialog because the template’s workflow needs Git. {template} is its name.

git.vc.useParent.description: Button on Git’s page in the Version Control tab of a project inside another repository: switches the project to Git on that repository, after the warning (the … says it asks first: keep it).

git.vc.workflow.defaultMessage: Workflow: {platform} · {state, select, preset {{preset}} custom {Custom (from {preset})} other {no preset chosen}}
git.vc.workflow.description: A link atop the Version Control tab: the project’s workflow, its version control ({platform}: None or Git) and its preset ({preset}: Solo, Pair, Team); Custom when the options were changed after it. Opens the Workflow section. Glossary 2.1: workflow, preset, Custom.

git.vc.workflowTip.description: Tooltip of the "Workflow: Git · Team" link atop the Version Control tab.

git.worktree.agent.description: A worktree that belongs to an agent. {agent} is the agent's name.

git.worktree.badge.description: Badge on a branch checked out in a worktree that isn't an agent's.

git.worktree.slotLease.defaultMessage: {kind, select, card {{slot}: {agent} on {card}} lane {{slot}: {agent}, lane {lane}} carried {{slot}: carried, agent {agent}} other {{slot}: not lent}}
git.worktree.slotLease.description: A slot's row in Git → Branches & remotes, Worktrees (#1450): its name and its lease: lent to an agent ({agent}) for a card ({card}: its key) or a lane ({lane}: its name), carried for an agent (its old worktree, adopted), or not lent. carried: a noun before the name (glossary §1 rule 4).

git.worktree.unused.description: A worktree of the repository that belongs to no agent.

git.worktrees.changes.description: Button on a worktree's row: shows its changes in Git → Changes.

git.worktrees.copiesHeading.description: A heading in Git → Branches & remotes, followed by how many: the worktrees Combwork keeps for reviews (review copies: clean checkouts at the revision a reviewer checks). Combwork's own, not the user's.

git.worktrees.copiesHint.defaultMessage: Clean checkouts Combwork keeps for reviewers, each at the revision being checked. Combwork manages them: there is nothing to remove here.
git.worktrees.copiesHint.description: Under the Review copies (Combwork's) heading in Git → Branches & remotes.

git.worktrees.copyRow.defaultMessage: {use, select, review {{copy}: {agent} reviewing {card} at {revision}} check {{copy}: {agent} checking {card} at {revision}} other {{copy}: idle in the pool}}
git.worktrees.copyRow.description: A review copy's row in Git → Branches & remotes: its name ({copy}, such as copy-1, keep it as it is) and who uses it: a reviewer ({agent}) reviewing a card ({card}: its key) at a revision ({revision}: a short commit id), an agent running a check on it, or no one (idle in Combwork's pool of copies). Keep the select keys.

git.worktrees.heading.description: Heading in Git → Branches & remotes, followed by how many there are.

git.worktrees.queueHeading.description: A heading in Git → Branches & remotes, followed by how many: the folder Combwork's merge queue tests merges in (glossary: merge queue). Combwork's own, not the user's.

git.worktrees.queueHint.defaultMessage: Where Combwork’s merge queue tests a card’s merge before it goes in. Combwork manages it: there is nothing to remove here.
git.worktrees.queueHint.description: Under the Merge queue (Combwork's) heading in Git → Branches & remotes.

git.worktrees.queueRow.description: The merge queue's folder's row in Git → Branches & remotes (glossary: merge queue).

git.worktrees.readOnly.defaultMessage: Read-only here: an agent's work comes into the project folder through Merge.
git.worktrees.readOnly.description: Under the Worktrees heading. Merge is the name of the action that brings an agent's branch in.
